_README: The 'descent' rail on the home page. As the reader scrolls down the page they go down into the Earth,
and each stop is an instrument from your career, ordered by the pressure it reaches.
pt      its pressure and temperature reach, as you would say it
depth   the depth in the Earth that pressure corresponds to (km); the readout counts up to it
where   what is there (one or two words)
color   the colour the rail turns at that stop (cool at the surface, incandescent at the core)
Keep them in order of increasing pressure. The first entry is the surface.

Keep them in order of increasing pressure. The first entry is the surface. A stop may go beyond the Earth: give it 'gpa' and 'tc' (its pressure in GPa and temperature in °C) and 'planet': 'jupiter' and the cutaway Earth gives way to that planet.
earth.layers   the layers drawn in the cutaway, with top and bottom depth (km) and colour.
earth.profile  depth (km) -> pressure (GPa) and temperature (°C) inside the Earth, used for the gauges (PREM + a typical geotherm).

The terapascal figure is from Dubrovinskaia et al., 'Terapascal static pressure generation with ultrahigh yield strength nanodiamond', Science Advances 2, e1600341 (2016) — double-stage DAC, Bayreuth.
